# Learnings

Append-only. One dated line per non-obvious lesson from a finished task that is not visible in the code itself, with the task ID (lessons inherited with the repository foundation carry the area they came from instead). `/plan` reads this before scoping similar work. Promote a line to the **Gotchas** section of `AGENTS.md` only if every future task must respect it; delete lines that stop being true.

- 2026-09-17 (tracking): Beads 1.3.0 stores issues in an embedded Dolt database and writes Codex/Cursor config plus git hooks on `bd init`; Backlog.md keeps one markdown file per task and its agent guides inside the CLI (`backlog instructions ...`), which is why it was chosen (ADR-0001).
- 2026-09-17 (browser tooling): `@playwright/test` 1.63 already bundles the agent CLI, MCP server, trace inspector and skills; the standalone `@playwright/cli` and `@playwright/mcp` pin an alpha Playwright with its own browser build, so never install them alongside.
- 2026-09-17 (browser tooling): Vercel agent-browser drops the zero-width non-joiner from Persian accessible names in snapshots; copy names only from Playwright snapshots.
- 2026-09-17 (browser tooling): the official Playwright container has no Persian UI font (falls back to FreeSerif); self-host the app's typeface or CI screenshots will never look like production.
- 2026-09-17 (browser tooling): `playwright install` garbage-collects browser builds no installation references, including other projects' on the same machine; use `pnpm browsers`, which passes `--no-remove`.
- 2026-09-17 (browser tooling): a credential scrubber keyed on parameter names alone will redact the page URL itself (analytics send it as `session…=`); require values to look opaque before scrubbing.
- 2026-09-18 (design harness): a new file in `.claude/agents/` is not callable as a subagent type immediately (the Agent tool answered "not found" right after the file was written and registered it a few minutes later); if it is unknown, run the same prompt through a general-purpose subagent instead of waiting.
- 2026-09-18 (design harness): `Intl` for `fa-IR` has three traps: `dateStyle: 'full'` prints «۱۴۰۵ شهریور ۲۷, جمعه», the `currency` style puts «ریال» before the number, and `NaN` renders as «ناعدد»; format with `long` plus your own weekday, append the unit yourself, and treat «ناعدد» on screen as a bug.
- 2026-09-18 (design harness): model vision cannot see a 2 px shift (0.07 % of pixels in a 160×60 box); measure spacing, sizes and contrast from the DOM (`playwright cli snapshot --boxes`, `eval`) and use screenshots only for gross problems.
- 2026-09-21 (react harness): path-scoped rules in `.claude/rules/` attach only when a matching file is opened with the Read tool; a fresh session that read code with `cat` or only created files got none of them, so the AGENTS.md map and `/work` name the packs explicitly.
- 2026-09-21 (react harness): Vitest without `globals` never runs Testing Library's automatic cleanup (a second render in a file sees the first); register `cleanup` in `vitest.setup.ts`. `import 'server-only'` resolves in Next builds but not in Vitest; alias it to `next/dist/compiled/server-only/empty.js`.
- 2026-09-21 (gorilla tests): fast-check's `interruptAfterTimeLimit` resolves while the run in flight keeps driving the page; with Playwright, enforce the time box between runs. A time box also makes a fixed seed machine-dependent, so anything that must be deterministic counts runs instead.
- 2026-09-26 (CS-1): robots.txt is not permission: Divar's robots.txt only blocks a few paths, but its terms of use forbid any automated copying of listings, and Karnameh allows listing pages while disallowing their photos; read the terms and the robots rules per source before crawling (ADR-0008).
- 2026-09-26 (CS-1): torob.com answers automated clients with its own CAPTCHA (HTTP 490); study Torob from archived pages, its engineering blog and its careers API, never by crawling it.
- 2026-09-26 (CS-1): a capture that succeeds can still be a block page: DataDome answered a CarGurus results page with HTTP 200, then laid «Access is temporarily restricted» over an intact DOM, so the accessibility tree and the tokens looked normal and only the screenshots showed it. Open the first-view screenshot before trusting any capture; the tool now also stops on requests to challenge-only hosts (`captcha-delivery.com`).
- 2026-09-26 (CS-26, CS-27): the App Router renders with Next.js's bundled React canary, not the React in `package.json`, while Vitest uses the one in `package.json`; with the pin at 19.2.8, `<ViewTransition>` worked in pages but was missing in unit tests. When a React API behaves differently in tests and pages, compare `next/dist/compiled/react` with the pinned version (CS-27 moved the pin to 19.3.0).
- 2026-09-26 (CS-26): a skeleton that renders the component's own frame still drifted: on a 412 px phone the real facts line wrapped and rows came out 20 px taller, and a 4:3 thumbnail in a flex row stretched to the row's height (stretch overrides `aspect-ratio`). Give every slot a fixed line count and aspect frames `self-start`, then measure both row heights.
- 2026-09-26 (CS-26): behind `useOptimistic`, `revalidateTag(tag, 'max')` made a saved bookmark jump back 451 ms after the tap (stale-while-revalidate sends no re-render), and a reload still served the stale value; `updateTag` held. Every action behind an optimistic control uses `updateTag` or `refresh()`.
- 2026-09-26 (CS-26): `playwright cli run-code --filename` wraps the file in parentheses and runs it in a bare VM context: the file must be one function expression with no trailing semicolon (so it is in `.prettierignore`), and outside `page.evaluate` there is no `console` or `setTimeout`.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-28): in Next.js 16.3 with Cache Components, a page that reads `params` or uncached data outside Suspense fails `next build` with a blocking-prerender error unless it exports `instant = false`; the dev overlay calls the same thing an "insight", and the instant-navigation docs say validation leaves the build unaffected, which misled a first reading. A page that must answer a real 404 (a listing) is exactly such a blocking page.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): PGlite 0.5.8 runs PostgreSQL 18.3 but is built without lz4, so a column declared `COMPRESSION lz4` fails in the schema tests; compression is a server setting (`default_toast_compression` in `db/postgresql.conf`), never column DDL.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): a host `pg_dump` older than the server aborts, and dbmate then skips its schema dump without failing the migration; dump through the container (`scripts/db.sh`), never with the host's tools.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): BEFORE triggers run before CHECK constraints, so a row that breaks both fails with the trigger's name (`listing_status_guard`), not the constraint's; tests that expect a constraint name must know which fires first, or disable the trigger inside the test's transaction.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): the Write tool refuses `.env.example` because of the `Read(./.env.*)` deny rule, so the settings template is `example.env`, which agents can keep current; `.env` itself stays unreadable.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): a hook's `permissionDecision: "deny"` holds in bypass-permissions mode, while the docs do not say whether `"ask"` does; the database guard denies, and it matches commands at the start of a command segment, because matching anywhere refused an edit whose text only mentioned `docker compose down -v`.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4): edit an unmerged migration only after rolling it back: dbmate undoes a migration with the file's current down section, so after editing migration 3 its new down section dropped a trigger the applied version never had, and rollback failed; restoring the old down section long enough to roll back fixed it.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-4 review): a CHECK passes when its expression is NULL, so `access_method <> 'crawl' OR min_request_interval_ms >= 3000` accepted a crawled source with no interval at all; and a BEFORE INSERT trigger fires on the row an upsert proposes before the conflict is found, so the lifecycle guard refused a re-crawl that turned an active listing sold. Both were found by the database-reviewer, not by the tests written alongside the schema.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-2): Jalali libraries must be tested in both directions and pinned by a test: `jalaliday` 3.1.1 turns Jalali into Gregorian correctly but puts every 1 January to 29 February of a Gregorian leap year a day ahead going the other way, and ICU 77+ (Node 22.23+, 24, 26; Chrome 148+) moved dates from 2124-03-20 onward relative to ICU 76, so a runtime upgrade can change the calendar. The lab in `docs/research/2026-09-27-money-and-jalali-calendar/lab/` checks both.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-2): adding a column of a constrained domain rewrites the table on PostgreSQL 18 (its file node changed), while a nullable column with its own CHECK does not; give shared rules a CHECK per column, as amounts do.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-2 research): WebFetch's page summariser misreports Unicode separators (it called an ASCII comma U+066C); settle character-level facts from raw bytes (a public capture or `curl` into the scratchpad), never from a summary.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): a sign read after a number («٪», «%», «‰», «°») shows on the wrong side of Persian digits: they are bidi class EN, so UAX #9 rule W5 pulls the sign into their left-to-right run, and `Intl`'s «۱۲٪» renders with it on the right. `formatPercent` puts U+200F before the sign; judge such fixes by measured glyph positions (`inspectLayout`), because reading the order off a small screenshot misled the review once.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): `font-display: optional` is not free in a single-page app: after a slow first load the fallback stays for the whole visit, client-side navigations included (measured 197.4 px against 213.0 px for the same text). Swap with preload cost at most CLS 0.033 with the font 1.5 s late.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): Playwright reads an array passed to `test.use` as a `[value, options]` fixture tuple, so `ignoreBrowserErrors: [/a/, /b/]` arrives as the single RegExp `/a/`; pass `[[/a/, /b/], { scope: 'test' }]`.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): with `better-tailwindcss/no-unknown-classes`, the plugin also reads string-literal types inside a `classes` variable, so `satisfies Record<Level | 'none', string>` reports `none` as an unknown class; declare the type alias outside the variable.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): Tailwind 4 still generates `leading-none`, `leading-<n>`, `duration-<n>` and `delay-<n>` from bare values after the theme's line-height and duration scales are removed, and `no-unknown-classes` accepts them; only `no-restricted-classes` patterns stop them from overriding a role's line height or the motion tokens.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3 review): a bare `--update-snapshots` means `changed`, which keeps every image inside `maxDiffPixelRatio` (1%), so the committed `/design` baselines still showed «٪» on the wrong side after the fix. Regenerate with `--update-snapshots=all`, and guard glyph-level details with measured checks (`inspectLayout`), not full-page screenshots.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3 review): `wrap-anywhere` on a Persian string breaks inside a word once a no-break space has made the amount and «تومان» one unit («توما» and «ن» at 320 px). Only digit runs may carry it (`NumericText`), and `inspectLayout` reports Persian words split across lines.
- 2026-09-27 (CS-3): with Cache Components, Next.js 16 keeps the route you left mounted in a hidden `<Activity>`, so after leaving an error screen its `h1` is still in the DOM. Query by role, which sees only visible elements, not by tag.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-5): find a source's terms through its footer, never a remembered address. Divar's moved to a help article that renders only in a browser (plain HTTP gets an empty shell, the 2026-09-26 address answers 404), Karnameh's general terms live at `/car-inspection/terms`, and Sheypoor's footer link opens an FAQ with no terms.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): with Cache Components, Next.js wraps `Date`, so a logger that stamps lines with `Date.now()` inside a render counts as dynamic input; stamp with `performance.timeOrigin + performance.now()`, as Next.js's own span store does.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): Next.js sets `Error.prepareStackTrace`, so `error.stack` stays unmapped even under `--enable-source-maps`; map frames yourself with `module.findSourceMap()`, which works once source maps are enabled (the flag, or `process.setSourceMapsEnabled(true)` before the code loads) and returns nothing otherwise.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): Turbopack names a browser chunk's source map by its own hash (`23-cxwomf0no7.js` ends with `//# sourceMappingURL=3y_lez0yndito.js.map`); find a map through the chunk's comment, never by appending `.map`.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): `instrumentation.ts` is also built for the Edge runtime, and only a literal `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME` check lets Next.js drop Node-only imports from that build; behind a getter it compiled pino into it (72 compile errors in `next dev`), and the owner's long-running dev server then failed instant validation («Cannot access "moduleLoading" without a work store») on every page until restarted.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): a page that reads `params` at the top with `instant = false` and no Suspense above was still built as a partial prerender (◐) and answered 200 with `noindex` for both `notFound()` and a thrown error; check the status in a browser test before relying on a real 404 (CS-64).
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): with `reactCompiler: true`, a client component's browser source map points at the compiler's output, not our file (its content starts with `react/compiler-runtime`), so mapped browser stacks were off by a few lines, and a hoisted event handler's by 18. Matching lines by text fails (the compiler reprints strings and JSX); running Next.js's own compiler step again with Babel's maps on reproduces the output byte for byte and gives the exact map (`apps/web/scripts/browser-source-maps.mjs`). Server maps are not affected.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): Next.js serves `/_next/static` and `public` files before its traced handler, so they start no span; anything keyed off Next.js's spans (the `request completed` line) misses them unless something below Next.js, such as a hook on `http.Server`'s `emit`, fills in.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): on Node 22.14 Next.js compiles `next.config.ts` to CommonJS, so an `await import()` inside it becomes `require()` and fails on a `file://` URL; import a helper script statically (`require` of an `.mjs` works from Node 22.12).
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): anything that runs on every request line runs on attackers' text. A regex with an unbounded run (`[\w.-]*`) retried from every position made a 16 KB request path take 350 ms to log, and ten such requests stalled the server for seconds; bound every repetition, read only what can be shown, and cut text only after redacting it (a secret cut in two matches no pattern, and 10 of a phone number's 11 digits showed).
- 2026-09-28 (CS-30): when the visitor leaves before a Route Handler answers, Next.js 16.3.5 usually ends the root span once the handler is done (the route and status are set only then), and sometimes never does. Ending it yourself at the response's `close` loses them; mark it then and end it only after a grace period (the http.Server hook in `packages/observability/src/tracing.ts`).
- 2026-09-28 (CS-31): VS Code lints every workspace package in one ESLint process, and reading `tseslint.configs` records the reading config's folder as a candidate tsconfigRootDir in a process-wide set; with two package configs loaded, any file parsed without an explicit `tsconfigRootDir` fails with "multiple candidate TSConfigRootDirs", in the editor only, since `pnpm lint` gives each package its own process. Set it for every file a config lints; the lint self-test lints in one process to catch it.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-31): in a window opened from a workspace file, even one holding a single folder, VS Code ignores that folder's window-scoped settings (`typescript.tsdk`, `files.associations`, `prettier.documentSelectors`); only resource and language settings apply. Open the folder itself, or put those in the workspace file.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-31): Claude Code's typescript-lsp plugin reports "new diagnostics" from a long-lived typescript-language-server (global TypeScript) that misses edits made through Bash and git; a session was shown errors from CS-30's intermediate states that no longer existed on disk. `pnpm typecheck` is the reference.
- 2026-09-28 (CS-31): VS Code's diagnostics can be read without a person clicking through files: run the installed VS Code as an extension test host (`--extensionDevelopmentPath`, `--extensionTestsPath`) with its own `--user-data-dir` and linked extensions, open each file in a tab, and read `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics`; a tsserver request (`typescript.tsserverRequest`, `semanticDiagnosticsSync`) waits for the project to load before the quiet period starts.
- 2026-09-28 (backlog re-planning): `backlog task view --plain` prints the Definition of Done with the same `- [ ] #n` markers as the acceptance criteria, so a script that reads criteria back from it and passes them to `--acceptance-criteria` turns the three DoD items into criteria (it happened on CS-33); cut the text at `Definition of Done:` or read `--json`. Bulk task text holding apostrophes, backticks and Farsi goes through most safely as an argument array from a script with no shell in between (Node's `execFileSync`, for example), not through shell quoting: in zsh a `\'` inside single quotes ends the string, and the parse error created none of the tasks in that command.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): pg-boss's `groupConcurrency` counts active jobs per queue with a `NOT EXISTS` two fetches can both pass, and `localGroupConcurrency` is per process and per queue; neither holds a source to one job when its jobs sit in several queues or several processes. A `singleton` queue is exact across processes (a unique partial index, `job_i2`): one queue per source, and never a `singletonKey` on its jobs, which would give each key a slot of its own.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): pg-boss's exported install SQL (`getConstructionPlans`) creates today's and tomorrow's `pgboss.queue_stats_YYYYMMDD` partitions, so a migration made from it changes `db/schema.sql` every day and `pnpm db:check` fails the next morning. They serve only `persistQueueStats`; `pgboss:sql` leaves them out.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): in pg-boss, `retry_count` goes up when a job is claimed again, not when it fails: a job that failed once is `retry` with `retry_count` 0. And a job of a kind the claiming process does not know is not bad input: during a deploy the old worker claims the new kind's jobs from a shared lane, so it must put them back, not dead-letter them.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): a lane closes (in memory) while its request is recorded, before the job that met the refusal is put back or settled in pg-boss; a test that asserts on the queue right after seeing the lane close reads the job still `active` about one run in three. Wait for the queue state itself (`until`), never a fixed sleep.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): node-postgres returns a `timestamptz` of `'-infinity'` or `'infinity'` as the number `-Infinity` or `Infinity`, not a `Date`, while kysely-codegen still types the column as `Date`; a `DEFAULT '-infinity'` made `.getTime()` throw in the worker. Default to a real instant (`now()`) instead.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-32): pg-boss rebuilds bloated indexes only when its role is a member of the owner (`pg_has_role(current_user, relowner, 'USAGE')`), so PostgreSQL 17's MAINTAIN privilege does not switch it on for a non-owner worker; and two pg-boss processes polling one singleton queue at the same interval phase-lock, so one of them can run every job of a lane. Prove cross-process exclusivity with a direct `fetch()` from the second process while a job is active, not by expecting both to win jobs.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-42): on the owner's workstation, foreign destinations leave through a local transparent proxy that exits in the UK, so Cloudflare's trace says `loc=GB`. Iranian hosts such as Metis, AvalAI and GapGPT go through the ISP directly. To show that a request came from an Iranian network, time and trace the path to that host (`docs/research/2026-09-29-metis-ai/lab/network.mjs`); do not ask a foreign "what is my IP" service.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-42): Metis's OpenAI-format wrappers to Claude and Gemini (`/api/v1/wrapper/{anthropic,google}`) pass `response_format` on untranslated, and the provider refuses it. Structured output needs Metis's native `/anthropic` and Gemini routes. The DeepSeek route accepts only JSON mode, and `metis-gpt` wants `max_completion_tokens`.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-42): in a worktree-isolated Claude Code session, Claude Code refuses a Bash command that hands a computed value to git or backlog (`--plan "$(cat file)"`, a chained `node -e` program). Pass literal strings, or run a script from a file.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-36): the committed workflows start on the first push to a new GitHub repository (`e2e.yml` on every push to main and every pull request, `gorilla-nightly.yml` every night), and both build the app, which fails without the never-committed licensed typeface. Switch Actions off for the repository before the first push (`gh api -X PUT repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/permissions -F enabled=false`), and on again once CI provides the typeface (CS-38).
- 2026-09-29 (CS-43): Metis's published catalogue (`www.metisai.ir/models.json`) lags its live pricing endpoint, `GET https://api.metisai.ir/api/v1/meta/providers/pricing` (no key needed). On 2026-09-29 the catalogue priced gpt-5.6-luna at $0.10 and $0.60 per million tokens (OpenAI's batch price), while the endpoint said $0.22 and $1.32, about 1.1× list like every other model there. Price calls from the endpoint and reconcile with the invoice.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-43): through Metis, Anthropic's free `/v1/messages/count_tokens` answers 404, so Claude's tokens are counted from a Messages call's `usage`. And gpt-5.6-luna answers HTTP 400 ("Could not finish the message because max_tokens or model output limit was reached") when its reasoning uses up a small `max_completion_tokens`, instead of returning a truncated answer.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-44): `backlog task edit --ref` replaces the task's whole reference list, and `--add-ref` adds one. Two `--ref` calls silently dropped CS-44's link to CS-43's note until the full list was set again.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-44): in AI SDK 7, `generateText` with `Output.object` parses the answer only when the model stopped normally or wrote text. So a refusal or a truncation with no text returns a result whose `output` getter throws `NoOutputGeneratedError`: read `finishReason` first. `@ai-sdk/openai` also drops OpenAI's `refusal` field, so an OpenAI refusal arrives as an empty answer. A string model id goes to Vercel's AI Gateway. Telemetry records prompts and answers unless `recordInputs` and `recordOutputs` are off (`docs/research/2026-09-29-ai-layer-library.md`, section 6).
- 2026-09-29 (CS-39): Next.js 16 keeps the page just left in the document, hidden (Activity), so after moving from `/sign-in` to `/sign-up` both forms are in the DOM: an `id` used on both pages gave the visible input two labels and made `document.getElementById` find the hidden one. Field ids are unique per form. In Playwright, `getByLabel` also matches the hidden page's inputs (a strict-mode violation) while `getByRole('textbox', { name })` skips them; a password input counts as a textbox there.
- 2026-09-29 (CS-39): Playwright's WebKit on Linux (the `iphone` project) refuses every `Secure` cookie over plain http, on `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` alike, while Chromium and Firefox keep them; a `__Host-` session cookie would sign nobody in there. The session cookie drops the prefix and `Secure` only for plain http to a loopback host, decided per request, never by `NODE_ENV` (the e2e suite runs a production build over http).
- 2026-09-29 (CS-39): React 19 resets an uncontrolled form after its action, and a field keyed by the answer remounts empty; a test that fills the next attempt while the previous answer is still on its way loses what it typed. Wait for something only the new answer changes (the emptied password field), not for a summary whose text repeats.
